## Purpose

`golem-chain-intelligence` ingests blockchain blocks, tracks the active chain and network scope, and maintains snapshots of protocol state (liquidity, rates, contract conditions). It provides the foundation for Bardo Golems to query current on-chain reality.

## Key Invariants

- `#![deny(unsafe_code)]` — zero unsafe code; the crate will not compile otherwise
- `#![warn(missing_docs)]` — all public items require `///` doc comments
- Block data must reflect the authoritative chain state without corruption
- Chain scope must uniquely and correctly identify the target network
- Protocol state snapshots must return current on-chain conditions, never stale cached data

## Public API

This is a Plan 01 shell. Planned exports (from doc comment):

- Block ingestion interface — consume and parse new blocks
- Chain scope — query current chain ID and network identity
- Protocol state — snapshot queries for DeFi protocol conditions (rates, liquidity, contract health)

## Dependencies

None. Plan 01 creates the shell with empty `[dependencies]`. Later plans will add workspace crate dependencies as needed.

## Implementation Notes

- The doc comment mentions `bardo-witness` block ingestion and `PVS` — these imply coordination with a witness/oracle module and protocol viewing system, likely added in later plans.
- Chain scope should be injected at initialization, not hard-coded. Avoid embedding RPC endpoints or chain IDs in the crate.
- Protocol state must handle multiple DeFi protocols (Uniswap, Aave, Curve, Pendle, etc.) — use trait-based APIs instead of protocol-specific match arms.
- Block data structures should be minimal initially. Only parse and store what other crates actually consume.
- Chain scope likely interacts with `golem-heartbeat`'s tick system; plan for time-indexed state queries.

## Test Requirements

Tests live in `crates/golem-chain-intelligence/tests/` (integration) and inline in `src/lib.rs` (unit).

When concrete types are added, verify:

- Block ingestion does not corrupt transaction data (`test_block_data_integrity`)
- Chain scope correctly identifies the target network (`test_chain_scope_identification`)
- Protocol state queries return current on-chain values (`test_protocol_state_accuracy`)
- All public types have doc comment examples (required by `#![warn(missing_docs)]`)

## Do Not

- Add `unsafe` blocks; compile with `#![deny(unsafe_code)]`.
- Export types without doc comments; the crate rejects missing_docs.
- Hard-code chain IDs, RPC endpoints, or network names.
- Design for a single protocol; build for multi-protocol queries from the start.
